p.src: 1:1  In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

en: In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.
u.src: 1:1  In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.

p.src: 1:2  All praise be to Allah[1], the Lord[2] of the worlds[3],

en: All praise be to Allah[1], the Lord[2] of the worlds[3],
u.src: 1:2  All praise be to Allah[1], the Lord[2] of the worlds[3],

en:
[1] Allah is God’s most unique name.
 [2] The Arabic term "rabb" (translated as "Lord") includes all of the following meanings: "owner, master, ruler, controller, sustainer, provider, guardian and caretaker."
 [3] "the worlds" means mankind, jinn, and all that exists.

p.src: 1:3  the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful[4],

en: the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful[4],
u.src: 1:3  the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful[4],

en: [4] Ar-Rahmān and Ar-Raheem are two names of Allah: Rahmān is used only to describe Allah, while raheem might be used to describe a human as well. Rahmān carries a wider meaning - merciful to all creation. Justice is a part of this mercy. Raheem includes the concept of specialty - especially merciful to the believers. Forgiveness is a part of this mercy. In addition, Rahmān is adjectival, referring to an attribute of Allah and is part of His essence. Raheem is verbal, indicating what He does: i.e., bestowing and implementing mercy.

p.src: 1:4  Master[5] of the Day of Judgment.

en: Master[5] of the Day of Judgment.
u.src: 1:4  Master[5] of the Day of Judgment.

en: [5] Other meanings for "Mālik": Sovereign, Owner, etc.

p.src: 1:5  You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.

en: You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.
u.src: 1:5  You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help.

p.src: 1:6  Guide us to the straight path,

en: Guide us to the straight path,
u.src: 1:6  Guide us to the straight path,

p.src: 1:7  the path of those whom You have blessed[6]; not of those who incurred Your Wrath[7], or of those who went astray[8].

ar: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
en: the path of those whom You have blessed[6]; not of those who incurred Your Wrath[7], or of those who went astray[8].
u.src: 1:7  the path of those whom You have blessed[6]; not of those who incurred Your Wrath[7], or of those who went astray[8].

en:
[6] The way of the Prophets and those who follow them.
 [7] Those who know the Truth and do not follow it, like the Jews.
 [8] Those who are ignorant of the Truth and follow misguidance, like the Christians.
